nodes.name: Computer Organization and Architecture

topics.title: CPU design, instruction sets and pipelining

miniTasks: Design a half adder, full adder and a 4-bit counter on paper, then in a simulator.
Trace a small program through a 5-stage pipeline and mark every hazard.
Compute hit ratios and average access time for 10 cache problems.

resources.title: Nand2Tetris
resources.why: Build a computer from logic gates upward, connecting hardware concepts with software systems.

resources.title: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective
resources.provider: CMU / Randal E. Bryant & David R. O'Hallaron
resources.why: Strong systems foundation connecting machine representation, assembly, memory, linking, and performance.

resources.title: GATE Overflow – Computer Organization & Architecture
resources.why: Organizes GATE-relevant COA concepts such as addressing modes, memory hierarchy, pipelining, I/O, and performance into a focused subject reference with problem-solving guidance.

resources.title: Nand2Tetris Project 1 – Boolean Logic
resources.why: Requires learners to implement and test a complete set of basic logic gates from primitive NAND, turning digital-logic concepts into an executable hardware-design task.

resources.title: Gate Smashers – Computer Organization and Architecture Complete Playlist
resources.why: Specific COA playlist from Gate Smashers, suitable for GATE-focused coverage.

resources.title: Gate Smashers – Digital Logic Complete Playlist
resources.why: Specific digital-logic playlist for Boolean algebra, gates, combinational and sequential concepts.

resources.title: MIT OpenCourseWare – 6.004 Computation Structures
resources.why: Connects digital logic, processors, memory, assembly, and computer architecture so learners understand how software maps onto hardware.

resources.title: 15-213 Introduction to Computer Systems
resources.why: CMU’s systems course covers data representation, machine-level code, memory hierarchy, linking, exceptional control flow, and system-level programming.

resources.title: CS107 Computer Organization & Systems
resources.why: Builds strong understanding of C, pointers, memory, machine representation, assembly, and performance-oriented systems programming.

resources.title: Nand2Tetris Project 2 – Boolean Arithmetic
resources.why: Implementing arithmetic and logic chips turns Boolean algebra into a working ALU and reinforces digital-computer foundations.

resources.title: Nand2Tetris Project 3 – Memory
resources.why: Build memory chips from lower-level components to understand registers, RAM hierarchy, and addressing.

resources.title: Nand2Tetris Project 4 – Machine Language
resources.why: Writing assembly programs for the Hack platform connects instruction sets, registers, memory addresses, and control flow.
